column1: # WHY: the suite was 629s because four files grew to 66% of it. A one-time split decays;
# this table is the discipline made durable. Seeded from the measured post-shard run,
# rounded up to the next multiple of 5 plus a 5s margin (min 10s).
# A new tests/test_*.sh with NO row here fails tests/test_runtime_budgets.sh. That is
# deliberate: adding a test file is a conscious placement decision. Read tests/README.md
# before adding one — the usual right answer is to EXTEND an existing shard.
# NO row may exceed 60 seconds. If a file outgrows its ceiling, shard it or move the new
# assertions into a shard with room. Raising a number here is not the remedy, and it is not
# a quiet edit either: tests/test_runtime_budgets.sh pins the SUM of every ceiling in this
# table (EXPECTED_TOTAL), so a raise of any size reddens whether or not it breaks the 60s
# ceiling. The total does legitimately move when a new test file brings its own row, or when
# a sharded file's rows are re-cut — re-seed it from a measured serial run and say which.
# tests/test_docket_status.sh was raised 45 -> 50 by change 0118. It measured 45.15s STANDALONE
# SERIAL before the change — already AT PARITY with its own row, passing only on the runner's
# slack factor — and 0118 adds two sweep runs plus three fault-injection runs to the one file that
# owns sweep_execute coverage. Per this header's rule, from the WORST of three standalone serial
# readings after the change (44.55s; the other two were 43.76s and 44.22s): the next multiple of 5
# is 45, plus the 5s margin -> 50, which leaves 5.45s of headroom and stays clear of the 60s
# ceiling. Sharding was considered and REJECTED HERE: changes 0268 and 0154 are both queued against
# this same file, and re-cutting shards is precisely the edit that cannot rebase cleanly past them
# — the shard belongs to whichever change can take the whole file, not to one adding five fixtures
# Raised again, 50 -> 60, by change 0118's review finding 2, which adds one more sweep run (a wedged
# shared worktree at the publish-deferred mark). Six standalone serial readings after it: 45.17,
# 46.79, 51.36, 50.52, 46.12, 45.14. The WORST of the first three is 51.36 -> next multiple of 5 is
# 55, plus the 5s margin -> 60. Be clear about what that number is: the fixture itself costs well
# under a second (the same file measured 44.72s standalone immediately BEFORE it was added), and the
# ~6s spread across six back-to-back readings is machine load, not this change. The rule takes the
# worst reading, so 60 is what the rule yields.
# THIS FILE IS NOW AT THE 60s CEILING. There is no next raise. The next change that adds runtime
# here — 0268 and 0154 are both queued against it — must SHARD the file first; that is now the only
# available move, and it was already the header's stated remedy.
